summary: Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and doctoral supervisor Genjun Sasaki. He held positions at Otani University, attested between 1976 and 2002, and at JSPS in 1972.

Nora Kershaw Chadwick was an archaeologist, historian, and linguist who studied at Newnham College (~1911–1914). She held posts at the University of St Andrews and the University of Cambridge (~1950–1958).
Norbert Brox was a religious studies and history/archaeology scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Graz (~1969–1978) and the University of Regensburg (~1978–2000).

Norbert Samuelson was a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at Northwestern, HUC-JIR, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. His career included faculty posts at Brooklyn College, Rutgers, University of Virginia, Temple University (1975–1998), and Arizona State University (~1998–2016).

Noriaki Hakamaya is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Shun'ei Hirai and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He served as a long-time professor at Komazawa Junior College and Komazawa University.
Noriaki Hosoda is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at Hokkaido University (attested 1986 and 2003) and at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
Noriaki Inoue is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953) and later served as a professor there, attested in 1982.

Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku University, Bukkyo University, and Visva-Bharati University. He spent his career at Bukkyo University, serving as lecturer, associate professor, and professor between 1976 and 2021.
Norihiko Uchida is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held a post at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, attested in 1962.
Norihiro Matsuura is a scholar in history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held faculty posts at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society, both attested in 2026.

Norihisa Baba is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda. He held posts at Darwin College, Stanford, and the University of Tokyo, where he became professor in 2019.
Norio Fujisawa was a philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1953). He held a post at Kyoto University (~1957–1989) and served as Director of the Kyoto National Museum (~1993–2001).
Norio Harada is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology who studied at Ryukoku University. He held a professorship at Kyoto Women's University, attested in 1964.
Norio Koyama was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 2014.

Noritoshi Aramaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University. He held posts at Kyoto University, Osaka University, the Institute for Research in Humanities at Kyoto University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.

Noriyuki Kudo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Bukkyo University. He has held positions at Bukkyo University, the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology, and Soka University (attested 2000–2026).

Norman Fischer is a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied at Colgate, University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and Graduate Theological Union, and with teachers Sojun Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker. He founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.
Norvin J. Hein was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion at Yale Divinity School, attested in 1965.

Nosei Fuji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University. He has held posts at Daegu University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, Bukkyo University, the Institute of Religious Culture, and Ryukoku University.

Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served as Associate Director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions (1974) and held a post at the University of Oslo (~1986–2011).
